releases.body:
THE LANDMARK NEW YORK CITY CULTURAL INSTITUTION HAS CHAMPIONED THE WORK OF ARTISTS OF AFRICAN DESCENT FOR NEARLY 60 YEARS

HARLEM, N.Y., Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- To mark her birthday today, global entertainer, entrepreneur and art collector, Beyoncé, makes a $2 million gift to the renowned Studio Museum in Harlem. Founded in 1968, the New York City cultural institution is the nexus for artists of African descent locally, nationally, and internationally and for work that has been inspired and influenced by Black culture. Beyoncé has long been an art collector and a true fan of the Museum's mission of promoting multiple generations of artists of the African diaspora. 

"Art tells all our stories; the past and the present, but is not always accessible to everyone," says Beyoncé. "I have always been impressed with the Studio Museum in Harlem because of its intention to make the museum an integral part of the community. I have been introduced to several of my favorite young and upcoming Black artists through exhibits at the Museum. It is a place of inspiration where all audiences can discover new stories through the canvases of diverse storytellers that reflect our humanity."

Thelma Golden, Ford Foundation Director and Chief Curator of the Studio Museum in Harlem, said, "I am deeply grateful to Beyoncé, both for the generosity of this gift, especially on her birthday, and for recognizing the vital role that the Studio Museum plays in people's lives. Our institution was founded to shift the arts landscape and reimagine who that landscape serves. This gift will allow us to continue strengthening our work for Harlemites, New Yorkers, and audiences across the globe." 

About the Studio Museum in Harlem

Founded in 1968 by a diverse group of artists, community activists, and philanthropists, the Studio Museum in Harlem is internationally known for its catalytic role in promoting the work of artists of African descent. The Studio Museum's new home, situated at its longtime location on West 125th Street, opened to the public on November 15, 2025. Designed by Adjaye Associates with Cooper Robertson serving as executive architect, the building—the first created expressly for the institution's program—enables the Studio Museum to better serve a growing and diverse audience, provide additional educational opportunities for people of all ages, expand its program of world-renowned exhibitions, effectively display its singular collection, and strengthen its trailblazing Artist-in-Residence program.

For more information, visit studiomuseum.org.

Visitor Information 

The Studio Museum in Harlem is located at 144 West 125th Street, between Malcolm X Boulevard (Lenox Avenue) and Adam Clayton Powell Boulevard (Seventh Avenue). 

The Studio Museum is open Wednesday through Sunday, from 11:00 am to 6:00 pm, with extended hours on Friday, from 11:00 am to 9:00 pm.

The Museum is open to Members on Saturday mornings, from 10:00 to 11:00 am, before the galleries open to the public.

Admission rates are offered as a suggestion, with Sundays free for everyone. Suggested rates are $16 for adults and $9 for seniors (sixty-five years and over), students, and visitors with disabilities (care partners are free). Admission is free for children sixteen and under. 

Tickets to the Studio Museum may be purchased online at studiomuseum.org/visit or at the Museum.

releases.body:
Lawsuit alleges Suno built a name-indexed music platform that commercially exploits musicians' identities without consent, seeks to protect musicians' rights in the age of AI

CHICAGO, Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Korein Tillery has filed a new lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. The lawsuit is filed on behalf of acclaimed musician Jason Isbell and other music artists representing a proposed class of similarly situated musicians whose identities have been appropriated and commercially exploited without consent by AI music-generation platform Suno, Inc. The lawsuit asserts claims under a number of state right-of-publicity laws and the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act.

The case, Jason Isbell, et al. v. Suno, Inc., alleges that Suno designed, trained, and commercially deployed a platform built to retrieve musicians by name and provide a multi-media experience evoking those musicians' identities on command. The complaint includes dozens of demonstrations and exhibits of Suno providing—based on musicians' names alone—songs like one the named musician might make, descriptions of the musicians' attributes, and related images (e.g. a white glove for the artist Michael Jackson). According to the complaint, Suno provides these outputs for musicians whose talents span blues, rock, country, alternative, reggaeton, rap, pop, salsa, Hawaiian, ska punk, and alt-country-punk fusion. 

The lawsuit also alleges that Suno, without consent, created and stored voiceprints indexed by name when training its AI on musicians' voices.

"Despite its assertions that Suno did not train its AI on specific musicians' identities and does not allow artists' names as prompts, its own public-facing product shows otherwise," said George A. Zelcs, Partner at Korein Tillery. "Further, Suno's own licensing agreements with major music companies expressly recognize that a copyright license does not supply the separate consent required from the human creators whose identities have been commercially exploited. It's time for musicians to have a seat at the table. We will work vigorously to protect their right to control the use of their own identities." 

The Korein Tillery legal team on this matter includes George A. Zelcs, Audrey L. C. Austin, Marc Wallenstein, and Lucy Prather.

Korein Tillery is an AV-rated, award-winning law firm with offices in St. Louis, Chicago, and Naples. The firm has recovered billions of dollars in verdicts and settlements by aggressively pursuing complex civil cases. Korein Tillery has been named by the National Law Journal as one of the nation's top plaintiffs' law firms.

releases.title: Come Talk To ME, Featuring AI-Recreated Voice, Selected for Twin Cities Film Fest
releases.body:
Documentary brings Parkinson's conversations to film festivals and communities

MINNEAPOLIS, Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Come Talk To ME, the feature-length (76 min) documentary by independent filmmaker and director Deacon Warner and first-time producer Jackie Hunt Christensen, has been selected to be part of the Twin Cities Film Fest, Oct. 15-24. The film is also currently available for community screenings worldwide through Kinema, a streaming platform that allows groups to license the film for both in-person and virtual screenings.

Come Talk To ME follows Parkinson's disease (PD) activist Jackie Hunt Christensen, her husband Paul Christensen, their two sons, and a diverse group of friends with PD. Their stories reflect on the many types of communication that are necessary to participate fully in relationships as the disease progresses.

In a groundbreaking approach, Jackie uses artificial intelligence (AI) to recreate her voice as it sounded two years after her diagnosis in 1998 but before the disease had noticeably impacted her speech. This AI-generated voice, dubbed "JHC2K," asks questions written by Jackie's present-day self and also serves as the film's narrator. 

The documentary offers an intimate look at Jackie and Paul's journey, including reflections from their two now-grown sons on how 28 years of Parkinson's have shaped their family dynamic. It also captures Jackie's behind-the-scenes efforts to produce the film, including a trip to an international summit for Parkinson's support group leaders in Austin, Texas, where she and Paul conducted interviews.

Throughout the production, Jackie and Paul face new challenges, but Jackie remains deeply committed to completing the film and raising awareness about how Parkinson's impacts communication and relationships, particularly affecting care partners.

The filmmakers are especially eager for the film to be viewed in settings that allow post-screening discussions, such as film festivals and community-hosted screenings. "I showed [Come Talk To ME] to a group of 23. Every person in the room shared that it was relevant in their life. Everyone should see this," said screening host Kari Kielblock. 

Viewer Marna Anderson described the film as, "a realistic and beautiful look at a family who is learning to love more deeply through a painful and difficult disease. It also provided excellent information and resources for viewers."

Screening Details:

Come Talk TO ME screens at 12 pm on October 24 at Edina Mann Theatre (3911 W. 50th St.

Edina, MN 55424) as part of the Twin Cities Film Fest, which runs Oct 15-24. The Twin Cities Film Fest is headquartered at Marcus West End Cinema, 1625 Park Place Blvd., St. Louis Park, MN 55416.

Anyone interested in hosting a screening of Come Talk To ME can do so directly through the film's Kinema page. Prospective hosts can also contact the film's director: director@cometalktomefilm.com

Visit the film's website to learn more about the film, find Parkinson's disease resources as well as find information about hosting a screening: cometalktomefilm.com

About the Filmmakers

Producer Jackie Hunt Christensen became a Parkinson's disease activist when she was diagnosed with the disease. She has published two guide books on the disease, The First Year---Parkinson's Disease: An Essential Guide for the Newly Diagnosed (2005) and Life With a Battery-Operated Brain: A Patient's Guide to Deep Brain Stimulation Surgery for Parkinson's Disease (2009).

At the time she was diagnosed at 34, Jackie was Co-Director of the Food and Health program at the Institute for Agriculture & Trade Policy in Minneapolis, Minnesota, as well as a co-founder and Co-Director of Health Care Without Harm (HCWH): The Campaign for Environmentally Responsible Health Care. She continued working for both organizations until June 2004, when, at age 40, her PD symptoms forced her to leave her jobs and apply for disability benefits.

Director Deacon Warner is a documentary filmmaker and youth media instructor. He has been teaching media arts since 2008. As an independent filmmaker, Deacon has directed numerous short documentaries including Bee-Sharp Honeybee, Literacy for Freedom: Empowering Black Boys in MN and Every Day Is a Parade. Deacon's first feature documentary, The Co-op Wars, premiered at the Minneapolis St Paul International Film Festival in 2021.

From The Jim Henson Company and Heather Henson, "Jim Henson's Harmonious Hoopla" stars Henson performers Jordan Brownlee (television: Slumberkins; stage: Emmet Otter's Jug-Band Christmas), Aymee Garcia (television: Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock; stage: Wicked, Into the Woods), and Leslie Carrara-Rudolph (television: Muppets Tonight, stage: Puppet Up!, Wake Up Your Weird) as they perform memorable and iconic songs from the legacy of Jim Henson with a live band, puppets from Jim Henson's Creature Shop, and a lot of fun. "Jim Henson's Harmonious Hoopla" is from The Jim Henson Company and Heather Henson. About The Jim Henson Company

The Jim Henson Company has remained an established leader in family entertainment for over 70 years and is recognized as an innovator in puppetry, animatronics, and digital animation. The Company's most recent credits include the Amazon Kids+ series Jim Henson's Monster Dance, the PBS KIDS special Wowsabout, the hit holiday special for Apple TV The First Snow of Fraggle Rock, and the Emmy-nominated Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Road Trip for Disney+, as well as the Oscar®-winning Guillermo Del Toro's Pinocchio for Netflix, and the Emmy®-winning Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock for Apple TV. Other television credits include Slumberkins and Harriet the Spy for Apple TV; Dinosaur Train, Splash and Bubbles, and Sid the Science Kid all for PBS; Earth to Ned for Disney+; and the Netflix series Word Party and the Emmy-winning The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance. Iconic catalogue titles include Fraggle Rock, The Storyteller, Farscape, and the ground-breaking fantasy classics The Dark Crystal and Labyrinth.

Headquartered in Los Angeles with additional locations in New York and London, the Company is also home to Jim Henson's Creature Shop™, a pre-eminent puppet and creature-building group and industry leader in puppeteered digital animation, with international film, television, theme park, and advertising clients.

About Heather Henson

Heather Henson is a producer, puppet artist, and creative steward whose work centers on connection—to one another, to the natural world, and to the sense of wonder she grew up with through the Muppets. Through the Green Feather Foundation, she creates environmental puppet theater and fosters independent artists through Handmade Puppet Dreams, the Puppet Slam Network, and the Jim Henson Carriage House, where new puppet works are developed in collaboration with the Jim Henson Foundation. Her philanthropic and investment work supports Indigenous communities, environmental stewardship, regenerative initiatives, and creative projects that help build a more connected and sustainable world. Heather is President of the Jane Henson Foundation, Chair of the Jim Henson Legacy, and a shareholder and board member of The Jim Henson Company.

Shadows of the Past and The Future of Cities explore decades of challenge, growth and change across the late 20 th and early 21 st centuries

NEW YORK, Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- New York: A Documentary Film, the acclaimed series produced by Steeplechase Films and directed by Ric Burns and written by Burns and James Sanders, returns with two new films premiering Monday, September 21 and Tuesday, September 22 at 9pm on PBS (check local listings), pbs.org and the PBS App. Presenting a vivid portrait of New York's evolution and transformation over the last half-century, Shadows of the Past and The Future of Cities chronicle the story of America's largest city across more than 50 years of challenge, growth, and change. Shadows of the Past and The Future of Cities are featured as part of The WNET Group's The Story of New York collection exploring the stories and history that built New York City and the extraordinary people who continue to inspire the future of this world hub.

Shadows of the Past, explores the forces that shaped the city in the second half of the 20th century, as New York plunged into the most threatening period of decline and disorder in its history—only to rise again, thanks to a stunning drop in crime, to regain its place at the vanguard of world cities. The episode concludes in the summer of 2001, with New York, now remarkably safe and secure, unaware that a new threat from beyond its borders would soon threaten to undo all the progress of the previous decade.

The Future of Cities begins just after 9/11 and follows New York's efforts to recover under the new and untested mayoralty of Michael R. Bloomberg. Through rare archival footage and compelling interviews, the episode traces the aftermath of 9/11, the financial crisis of 2008, Superstorm Sandy in 2012 and the COVID-19 pandemic of 2020. Yet defying the doomsayers, the city also rebuilt itself in these years on a dramatic scale—economically, physically, and demographically—thanks to an astonishing influx of newcomers from around the world. The episode ends with the inauguration of Zohran Mamdani as mayor of New York in January of 2026.

Narrated by Tony Award-winning actor Robert Sean Leonard, and featuring an original score by Emmy Award-winning composer Brian Keane, Shadows of the Past and The Future of Cities are presented in high-definition 4K video and sound, and feature a combination of original cinematography, archival footage, still photography and interviews with leaders in government, academia and journalism. Featured interviewees include four former New York City mayors David Dinkins, Michael R. Bloomberg, Bill de Blasio and Eric Adams; New York-Presbyterian President (Emeritus) Dr. Steven Corwin; The New Yorker's Adam Gopnik; Columbia University Professor Kenneth Jackson; The New York Times' Wesley Morris, Michael Kimmelman and Dodai Stewart; New York magazine's Justin Davidson; Fordham University Professor Christina Greer; architect and urbanist Vishaan Chakrabarti; PBS journalist Ray Suarez; New York University Professor Suketu Mehta; and The New York Times columnist and a co-anchor of CNBC's Squawk Box Andrew Ross Sorkin; and Social Activist Claudia Romo Edelman.

"New York City has been the supreme laboratory of modern life for four hundred years now," said Burns. "It's an astonishing vortex of capitalism and democracy, innovation and change, openness and toleration, that more than any other city on earth has made itself home to all the peoples of the world. Its story over the past fifty years has been one of almost constant challenge and self-reinvention—and a testimony to the extraordinary resilience and boundless collective energies that have kept it at the forefront of world culture. We're thrilled to welcome viewers back for these amazing recent chapters in the city's history." 

"It has been a gratifying experience to bring our series up to the present day with these new episodes," said Sanders, the Emmy Award-winning co-writer and co-producer of the new films. "Not only are there so many compelling stories to tell about the city's last half-century—some surprisingly little-known—but many of the greatest themes of the original eight episodes—immigration, globalization, the city's astonishing capacity for economic and physical reinvention—have powerfully reasserted themselves in recent decades—often at a scale and with a force never before seen, even in the city's long history."   

The original eight-part, 17½-hour series—tracing the history of the city across four hundred years, since its founding by the Dutch in 1624—was the recipient of two Emmy Awards, four additional Emmy nominations, the CINE Golden Eagle, and the Alfred I. duPont-Columbia University award, and became one of the most-watched presentations in public television history. Knopf, features two new chapters corresponding to the new episodes, along with contributions by Adam Gopnik, Ester Fuchs, and Suketu Mehta, all of whom appear in these new films.

It simplifies camera-top monitoring, wireless focus pulling, and mobile director monitoring, reducing setup complexity and enabling a more efficient production workflow.

Jay Sun, Product Manager at Hollyland stated, "For professional productions, an accurate monitor is essential because every department needs a reliable visual reference on set. Even minor color differences can affect decisions and create problems later in post-production. With Pyro 7 Ultra's QD-LCD technology, crews can trust what they see during production with professional-grade color accuracy".

Pre-Calibrated Display with Broadcast-Grade Color Accuracy

At the heart of the Pyro 7 Ultra is a premium QD-LCD display that delivers broadcast-grade color quality and consistency required for professional productions.

Each monitor is Calman® pre-calibrated to achieve a ΔE <1.5, ensuring highly accurate color reproduction directly out of the box. The display offers 99% Rec.709 and 95% DCI-P3 color gamut, Gamma 2.4, and up to 1,500 nits of brightness, providing dependable monitoring even in bright environments.

For long-term consistency, users can quickly recalibrate the display using the Hollyland Color Calibrator holistic solution that doesn't require a PC or third-party calibration hardware.

HDMI and SDI interfaces support loop-through and cross-output. Camera control is supported on select camera models from Sony, Canon, Nikon, and ARRI, with responsive control of functions including shutter, aperture, ISO, white balance, and more.

Robust Wireless Performance with TWiFi

Powered by Hollyland's proprietary Twin-WiFi (TWiFi) technology, the Pyro 7 Ultra simultaneously utilizes two wireless bands to create a resilient dual-path connection. Automatic frequency hopping minimizes interference in congested RF environments, maintaining a stable connection.

The system enables wireless video transmission at ranges of up to 1 km (3,300 feet), with latency as low as 20 ms in Focus Mode. It also supports 4K60 video transmission via one transmitter to an unlimited number of receivers, making it ideal for productions requiring multiple monitoring positions.

Professional Monitoring with HollyOS

The Pyro 7 Ultra introduces HollyOS, Hollyland's next-generation operating system designed for fast-paced production environments. The intuitive interface offers direct display controls, customizable monitoring layouts, and an extensive range of professional image analysis tools.

A Unified Ecosystem for Multi-Camera Productions

Unlike standalone wireless monitoring solutions, the Pyro 7 Ultra is designed as part of Hollyland's broader Pyro ecosystem. It pairs with compatible Pyro transmitters, receivers, and monitors, allowing production teams to expand or reconfigure wireless monitoring workflows without interoperability concerns or production delays. The result is a reliable, flexible, and scalable system that adapts easily to productions of any size.

ORLANDO, Fla., Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Things I Didn't Do, the independent psychological thriller series created by filmmaker Thiago Kling, premiered Saturday, Aug. 8, at Regal Winter Park Village & RPX, welcoming a full-capacity audience for the debut of its pilot.

Presented by Kling Brothers Entertainment in collaboration with the Orlando Film Commission, the premiere brought together the series' cast, crew, filmmakers, media and community supporters for an evening celebrating the years of work behind the production.

Originally conceived in 2015, The Things I Didn't Do was ultimately brought to life in Central Florida, with local talent and production partners contributing to the project on both sides of the camera. The premiere offered an opportunity to recognize that collaborative effort while spotlighting the region's established and emerging film community.

"Having the premiere here in Orlando, surrounded by the people who helped make this project possible, was incredibly rewarding," said Thiago Kling, creator and writer of The Things I Didn't Do. "The response from the audience made the night special for the entire cast and crew. We're proud of what we created together and grateful to everyone who supported us along the way."

Directed by Fernando Tosetti, whose work has earned numerous honors, including Best Director at Campus Movie Fest (2019), Best Editing from Orlando Independent Filmmakers (2021), Best Cinematography from the Organization of Independent Filmmakers (2025), a Silver Telly Award for Videography (2026) and a Best Picture nomination at the Hollywood Florida Film Festival, the series brings together an accomplished creative team. Written by Julia Antuerpem, a former Disney, Globo and Netflix writer, Harvard-trained creative writer and author of award-winning screenplays recognized with more than 60 international honors.

The series follows Ethan, a withdrawn teenager struggling to find his place in the world. To cope with feelings of isolation, Ethan fills a secret notebook with disturbing drawings imagining the deaths of those who have hurt him. When the notebook disappears and the people inside it begin dying exactly as he imagined, Ethan is pulled into a chilling mystery that forces him to question what is real and who can be trusted.

Following its Orlando premiere, The Things I Didn't Do begins its next chapter as the filmmakers explore opportunities to continue production and bring the full series to life for new audiences.

BURBANK, Calif., Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CJ 4DPLEX, the world's leading entertainment technology and content company specializing in premium film formats, cinematic production, visual effects and immersive experiences, today announced that Sony Pictures' Spider-Man: Brand New Day has become the highest-grossing film of all time across its SCREENX and 4DX formats, generating more than $104 million in combined global box office.

In just 33 days, Spider-Man: Brand New Day surpassed the previous all-time CJ 4DPLEX global box office record established by Avatar: The Way of Water, which accumulated $103 million across its 228-day theatrical run. The unprecedented speed at which Spider-Man: Brand New Day reached the milestone underscores the growing global demand for differentiated premium theatrical experiences and the increasing value SCREENX and 4DX can deliver to filmmakers, studios and exhibitors.

Since its global release, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has drawn more than 6.7 million admissions across SCREENX and 4DX, playing more than 115,000 shows across 1,200 screens worldwide. The film has achieved a record 40% average occupancy rate, demonstrating extraordinary audience demand and the ability of premium formats to drive moviegoers to theaters and maximize the value of every auditorium. It also set opening records for SCREENX in 36 countries and 4DX in 22 countries.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day marked the debut of CJ 4DPLEX's "Shot for SCREENX" initiative and the first time the company collaborated with filmmakers from on-set production through theatrical exhibition. Working alongside director Destin Daniel Cretton and the filmmaking team, SCREENX provided a new creative canvas designed to extend select moments beyond the traditional screen and surround audiences with imagery conceived specifically for the format, moving SCREENX further upstream in the creative process and giving filmmakers new tools to expand the scale and impact of their storytelling.

"The global response to Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been extraordinary," said Steven O'Dell, President, International Marketing & Distribution, Sony Pictures Entertainment. "The success of Shot for SCREENX demonstrates how creative collaboration can enhance the theatrical experience, and we're thrilled to see that innovation resonate with audiences around the world."

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day has achieved something no film has ever done across SCREENX and 4DX, and to establish this record in just 33 days makes the accomplishment even more extraordinary," said Jun Bang, CEO, CJ 4DPLEX. "As the first film in our Shot for SCREENX initiative, it represents an important evolution in how we collaborate with filmmakers and studios. We are incredibly grateful to Sony Pictures, Destin Daniel Cretton and the entire filmmaking team for embracing this new creative approach and helping demonstrate what is possible when premium formats become part of the filmmaking process from the beginning."

"This record demonstrates the tremendous opportunity premium formats create across the theatrical ecosystem," said Don Savant, CEO, CJ 4DPLEX Americas. "For studios and filmmakers, SCREENX and 4DX provide differentiated ways to showcase their biggest films, create excitement and drive incremental box office. For exhibitors, they provide a premium experience audiences actively seek out and are willing to pay more to enjoy. Most importantly, we are incredibly grateful to Sony Pictures for embracing our vision for 'Shot for SCREENX' and working with us to make it a reality. Their partnership and commitment were instrumental in achieving this historic success."

With SCREENX and 4DX now reaching audiences across major theatrical markets worldwide, studios and filmmakers have a powerful global premium platform through which to differentiate major releases, while exhibitors can offer audiences experiences that cannot be replicated at home.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now playing in SCREENX and 4DX theaters worldwide.

It's a BRAND NEW DAY for Peter Parker. Fighting crime full-time as Spider-Man in a world that doesn't remember him—and the pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him—sparks a change in Peter he may not have the power to control. releases.title: Dance Legends Armin van Buuren and Laidback Luke Join Moises to Build Responsible AI Tools for Musicians
releases.body:
Electronic pioneers will help shape new DJ and producer workflows for the creative suite used by 80 million musicians

SALT LAKE CITY, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Moises, the creative suite for musicians, today announced that Armin van Buuren and Laidback Luke have joined the company as the first members of its Artist Partnerships program. Both artists will help shape new producer- and DJ-focused features and contribute to conversations about the future of music technology and responsible AI. The new program follows the appointment of Charlie Puth as Moises' Chief Music Officer and expands the company's effort to put working artists at the center of how its creative tools are built.

At a time when generative AI is raising questions around consent, ownership, and replacement, Moises is taking a different approach: rather than generating finished songs from prompts, its creative suite helps musicians practice, perform, and create while keeping artistic decision-making in their hands. The company trains its AI models only on licensed and authorized content.

"Electronic music has always moved forward because artists were willing to experiment with new technology," said Geraldo Ramos, founder and CEO of Moises. "The next generation of creative tools has to be built with musicians, not around them. Armin and Luke understand the craft, the community, and the responsibility that comes with building tools musicians will actually use."

Architects of Modern Dance Music

For more than two decades, van Buuren has shaped the sound, culture, and worldwide reach of electronic music. One of only three artists to be named the world's No. 1 DJ by DJ Mag five times, he is a GRAMMY-nominated artist, co-founder of Armada Music, and host of A State of Trance, the radio show that reaches more than 40 million listeners.

"Technology has always been part of how electronic music evolves," said van Buuren. "What matters is whether the artist stays in control. Moises approaches AI with respect for the musician's own sound and decision-making, and I'm excited to help build tools that make producers faster and more expressive without taking the creativity out of their hands."

Laidback Luke is a DJ, producer, label founder, and educator whose influence helped shape the rise of modern EDM. Through Mixmash Records, his production forums, and masterclasses, he has championed emerging artists including Avicii and Afrojack. His collaboration and remix credits include Daft Punk, Kanye West, Rihanna, Madonna, Jay-Z, Pharrell, and others.

"Every generation of producers gets new tools, but the best tools do not do the work for you," said Laidback Luke. "They help you hear more, learn faster, and make stronger creative decisions. That is the kind of AI I want young producers to grow up with."

What Comes Next

Moises chose dance music as the starting point for the program because electronic artists have long been among the first to transform new technology into new forms of musical expression. Over the coming months, the company plans to announce additional high-profile artists and producers across multiple genres.

The program builds on the company's recent industry partnerships, including Fender, which selected Moises as the first AI technology partner for its Studio Pro DAW, and Ableton, which chose Moises' stem-separation technology for Ableton Live. Moises has also partnered with Blackstar Amps, the Whitney Houston Estate, and Cory Henry.

Learn more: https://moises.ai 

About Moises

Moises is the creative suite used by 80 million musicians worldwide. The platform gives everyone from hobbyists to world-class artists studio-level tools to practice, perform, create, and collaborate across mobile, desktop, and web. "SOCAN has a responsibility to act when the rights of music creators and publishers are put at risk. The evidence shows that the Suno platform has generated and streamed outputs that copy works in our repertoire, and that cannot go unchallenged," said Jennifer Brown, SOCAN CEO. "Innovation can't come at the expense of human creativity. The future of music must belong to the people who make it."

Suno has built its business by training its generative AI models on virtually all music files readily accessible on the Internet, without obtaining the necessary permissions or licences. SOCAN has identified Suno outputs that are identical or similar to songs in SOCAN's repertoire and have been generated and streamed without consent or compensation.

SOCAN's legal action is a necessary and proactive step to ensure that human music creation is valued, respected, and compensated.

Allegations of infringement

SOCAN's claim alleges that, by making the Suno platform available to the public in Canada, using it to generate and make available outputs that replicate songs in SOCAN's repertoire, and streaming those outputs to users in Canada and around the world, Suno has infringed SOCAN's performing rights in the underlying songs. The lawsuit lists a sample of 150 publicly available Suno outputs that SOCAN has identified. SOCAN expects other unauthorized outputs and activities to come to light as the litigation progresses.

"Suno's failure to meet its copyright obligations led us to pursue litigation," said Andrea Kokonis, Chief Legal Officer and General Counsel. "Our evidence is clear, and so is our objective: to establish that AI companies must respect the rights of music creators and publishers. This case is fundamentally about ensuring that long‑standing copyright principles continue to apply in the AI era."

SOCAN's action asserts that AI development must operate within the law and respect the rights of those who make music possible.

SOCAN will not comment on the claim beyond what is in the court record.

For more information visit the SOCAN litigation webpage.

SOCAN is Canada's largest member-owned music rights organization, championing the fundamental value of music and the people who create it. SOCAN collects license fees for the public performance and reproduction of music, matches them to rights holders, and distributes them as royalties to songwriters, composers and music creators and publishers in Canada and around the world. Boatlift 9/11 Named Best Short of the Season by Independent Shorts Awards

NEW YORK, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Great American Media commemorates the 25th anniversary of September 11 with the World Television Premiere of Original Film, Boatlift 9/11 (Boatlift 9/11), the award-winning short honoring the extraordinary mariners and ordinary citizens who answered an urgent call for help as Lower Manhattan came under attack. The film streams exclusively on Great American Pure Flix, beginning September 10.

Boatlift 9/11 honors the mariners who helped carry 500,000 to safety. Streaming Sept. 10 on Great American Pure Flix.

Twenty-five years after September 11, 2001, much of America knows the images and stories that have come to define that terrible day. Less widely known is what happened along the waterfront. As transportation out of Lower Manhattan shut down and thousands of people reached the water with nowhere else to go, ferries, tugboats, fishing boats and private vessels began moving toward them. More than 100 vessels ultimately joined the effort helping evacuate approximately 500,000 people in what became the largest maritime evacuation in history.

Inspired by Jessica DuLong's Saved at the Seawall, Boatlift 9/11 tells that history through Captain Jan and her daughter Britt, who are aboard their tugboat in New York Harbor when the first planes strike the World Trade Center. They race toward Battery Park, where survivors are stranded along the seawall. Their tug was never meant to carry crowds, but the pair begins pulling people aboard as smoke and ash consumed the waterfront. When Britt is swept into the river while trying to save another passenger, Jan faces an agonizing choice between searching for her daughter and getting those already aboard to safety. Jan and Britt eventually reunite and turn back toward Manhattan as the call goes out for "all available boats."

"I was in my office in New York, looking right down Sixth Avenue at an unimaginable tragedy as the second plane flew into the South Tower of the World Trade Center on September 11," said Bill Abbott, President & CEO, Great American Media. "Twenty-five years later, what remains equally vivid is what Americans did next. People ran toward the Towers to help people they did not know. Boatlift 9/11 tells one of the remarkable stories from that day, when hundreds of thousands of people found a way out of New York's lower west side because others chose to come for them, by boat. It is a story we are honored to be a part of producing and presenting on our platforms," Abbott concluded.

The film stars internationally acclaimed Swedish actress Sofia Helin (The Bridge, Atlantic Crossing) as Jan, with Preslea Elliott (Killers of the Flower Moon) as Britt and Hank Northrop ("Days of Our Lives," "Criminal Minds") as Eric. The film is directed by Dale Fabrigar. Written by Tricia Aurand. Produced by Suzanne DeLaurentiis, Nathan Samdahl, Dale Fabrigar, Nicole Menendez, David Courtice, and Christopher Dukes.

For producer Suzanne DeLaurentiis, Boatlift 9/11 is both a work of historical remembrance and an effort to preserve a part of September 11 history that many Americans have never known. An award-winning producer, writer and director whose career spans more than 100 film and television productions, DeLaurentiis has also long supported members of the military through her Operation Hollywood program, which helps veterans pursue careers in entertainment. She has received two U.S. military Commendation Medals for the work.

"Twenty-five years is an important threshold," said Suzanne DeLaurentiis. "There is now a generation of Americans who did not experience September 11 firsthand, and the responsibility to preserve these stories becomes greater with time. I wanted Boatlift 9/11 to remember the people who saw strangers in desperate need and simply went to get them. Half a million people made it off Manhattan by water that day. That extraordinary act of humanity deserves its place in our national memory," DeLaurentiis concluded.

Boatlift 9/11 has already received significant festival recognition. The Independent Shorts Awards International Film Festival named the film Best Short of the Season for June–July 2026. The film advanced to the festival's 2026 Annual Awards with nominations for Best Drama Short, Best Male Director for Dale Fabrigar, Best Supporting Actress for Preslea Elliott, Best Editing for Radu Ion and Best Original Score for Oliver Goodwill. The Annual Awards showcase will take place on September 19 at Regal LA Live in Los Angeles.

The film is presented by Suzanne DeLaurentiis Productions and the Mendez National Institute of Transplantation Foundation. Its commemoration of the boatlift also calls attention to the lasting health consequences experienced by people exposed to toxic debris following the attacks and the continuing need to support September 11 survivors. For more information on Kidney awareness and the Mendez National Institute of Transplantation Foundation visit MNITF.org.

Founded by corporate leader and philanthropist Sonia Jackson Myles, The Sister Accord® Foundation is dedicated to changing how girls and women treat, support and interact with one another. The weekend brought that mission to life through leadership, service, education, entrepreneurship, music and community.

The celebration began Saturday, August 29, with the Foundation's 36th Leadership Development Tea Party at Maketewah Country Club, featuring conversations focused on leadership, empowerment, service and wellbeing.

Five leaders were honored: Jonathan Butler, Grammy®-nominated singer, songwriter and guitarist; Courtis Fuller, Hall of Fame and multi-Emmy® Award-winning journalist; Patrick Lafley, Managing Partner & Co-Founder, Constellation Wealth Advisors; Commissioner Alicia Reece, Hamilton County Commission Vice President; and Amy B. Spiller, State President, Duke Energy Ohio and Kentucky.

Taylor Evans, a Cleveland Heights, Ohio native studying Middle Childhood Education at The Ohio State University, and Isley Mitchell, an Ohio State senior majoring in Psychology with a minor in Pharmaceutical Sciences, were named recipients of the Nella D. Jackson Memorial Scholarship, each receiving $5,000. Myles also announced an additional $5,000 scholarship opportunity for attendees.

Jean Freeman, Principal and CEO of Zambezi, announced a $50,000 donation to support the third cohort of The Sister Accord® Accelerator Program, launching later this year. Freeman and Myles will select seven women-owned businesses whose founders will receive coaching, mentorship and $10,000 business grants. Marchoe Dill Northern and Myles contributed an additional $10,000 each to support the program.

The Tea Party also featured a Duke Energy panel exploring the energy industry and the company's commitment to delivering power to the community, along with a conversation with Goodwill about service and its work supporting communities. Butler capped the event with a special performance.

The celebration continued Saturday evening with Butler performing at The Ludlow Garage. On Sunday, August 30, Stokley, the Grammy®-nominated singer, songwriter and producer known as the lead vocalist of R&B group Mint Condition and for his solo career, took the stage at The Ludlow Garage to close out the weekend.

The weekend led into The Sister Accord® Day on August 31, officially declared by the City of Cincinnati in 2013. The Foundation encouraged people to perform a random act of kindness for a girl or woman, extending its message of sisterhood beyond Cincinnati.

"This weekend was absolutely extraordinary! To see so many incredible people come together in the spirit of sisterhood, love, leadership and service was incredibly powerful," said Myles, Founder of The Sister Accord® Foundation. "The Sister Accord® has always been about what happens when we choose to lift one another up, and this weekend was a beautiful expression of that mission. I am so grateful to our honorees, partners, supporters and everyone who continues to believe in this work. Thirteen years after The Sister Accord® Day was first declared in Cincinnati, I am more inspired than ever about what we can accomplish together."

Myles thanked the event's sponsors, including Duke Energy, The Christ Hospital Health Network, bi3, Ohio Valley Goodwill Industries, Waymo, Porsche of The Village, Western & Southern Financial Group, Blockboard and Interact for Health.

BEIJING, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Swedish rock band The Cardigans led the lineup of nine international acts and 15 Chinese artists at the fifth Xiami Music & Arts Festival, held from Aug. 28 to 30, 2026. The three-day festival, themed "Life is not a track, but a ______," drew tens of thousands of fans to Aranya, a coastal cultural and tourism destination in northern China's Hebei province.

Co-produced by Damai Entertainment, an Alibaba Group subsidiary, and Aranya, and organized by Damai's Xiami Music Entertainment label, the festival has become one of China's major destination music events. Over the past five years, it has brought 33 international acts to China, introducing Chinese audiences to a broader range of music from around the world while providing overseas artists and music brands with a gateway to the Chinese market.

This year's international lineup featured artists from Sweden, the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia, including The Cardigans, Tortoise, The Horrors, Frente!, Gallant, Hayd, Christian Kuria, Ivoris and Zella Day. They performed alongside Chinese artists including Lao Lang, Chen Li and Leah Dou in a lineup spanning indie pop, post-rock, alternative rock, R&B and dream pop.

The Cardigans delivered a special 90-minute set featuring songs from across their three-decade career, including "Lovefool," "Communication" and "Carnival."

In recent years, the festival has expanded beyond music to include theater, exhibitions, film, designer toys and other forms of entertainment, becoming a showcase for Damai Entertainment's broader live entertainment portfolio. At this year's event, Damai Entertainment's designer-toy brand LUCKY LOOP showcased original characters including HEY PENNY, ECHOA and Kooie. The brand opened its first three stores—in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou—in August and plans to establish a presence in six Chinese cities by the end of the year.

The festival also highlighted the growing connections between Damai Entertainment's live entertainment and film businesses. The theme song and closing theme from the hit film Dear You were performed during the event. Damai Entertainment is also handling the film's worldwide theatrical release.

The festival's commercial program continued to grow in 2026, with 30 brands participating, including 88VIP, Samsung, Volkswagen, Tmall Hey Box, Tmall Super Brand Day, Sprite, Aimer, Freshippo and Nivea. Over the past five years, the festival has worked with 61 brand clients, 18 of which have returned for additional partnerships, representing a repeat-partnership rate of nearly 30%.

Environmental initiatives have also become an integral part of the festival's operations. Over the past five years, it has established 500 waste-sorting stations, collected more than 300,000 plastic bottles and engaged over 300,000 attendees in environmental initiatives.

About Damai Entertainment

Damai Entertainment is a technology-driven company delivering immersive, real-world entertainment experiences. Its diverse ecosystem spans film production, live events, IP commercialization, TV series, artist management, and ticketing platforms. Anchored in its dual strategic pillars of entertainment and AI, Damai is committed to creating unparalleled live, interactive, and immersive experiences for audiences around the world.

Fountain 0 Calls for Influencers with Major Social Media Followings to Join the Fountain 0 Talent Directory to be Eligible to Earn from Licensing Their Images

NEW YORK, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fountain 0 announced that Sunny Hostin, co-anchor of the acclaimed daily talk show The View, would become the first major personality to agree to develop and produce one or more films, and license her image and likeness for purposes of those films to the leading AI film and tv studio.

Fountain 0, which produced the first full length, live action film to be accepted at a major film festival, when it premiered at The Tribeca Film Festival last month, has also announced the release of its newest film, Odysseus: The Fall, in the very near future. The studio has gotten very significant national press for having produced content at a quality level comparable to traditional productions.

Odysseus: The Fall is using images of real people in the film, including Ash Koosha, the film's creator and CEO of Fountain 0 as Odysseus; Pooya Koosha, co-producer and co-founder of Fountain 0, as Eurylochus; and Tom Rogers, Executive Chairman of Fountain 0 and executive producer of the film, as Mentor.

Having demonstrated that the proprietary software and virtual production studio that Fountain 0 has built on top of AI video models is capable of reducing production costs to nominal levels while achieving the highest of quality productions, it has set its sights on ways to reduce marketing and promotion costs of its films. Along these lines, a key innovation that Fountain 0 intends to pursue is licensing the images of well-known personalities and influencers to represent characters in upcoming productions as a way to efficiently market releases to their followers. It has been proven for decades that recognizable personalities in films drive audience appeal, and to combine that with the power of social media relevance creates a formula to better enable audiences to know about films that incorporate the image of those they follow.

Sunny Hostin could not be a more perfect example of a very well-known figure to pioneer this new approach to incorporating the likenesses of key personalities into new films. Sunny not only has heavily devoted fans who enjoy her political, social, legal and cultural television commentary, while also having a major social media presence, but she is also a New York Times bestselling author, having written several books of fiction. In that regard, Sunny intends to bring her novels to the big screen through the industry leading AI film production capability of Fountain 0, while incorporating her own image in the film.

Ash Koosha stated, "This is obviously new territory for major talent personalities. We are incredibly gratified that Sunny is willing to be the talent pioneer willing to step out and take advantage of this new form of creative expression. Sunny, of course, will be able to decide which of her works she develops into a film, and what roles her image can be incorporated into under a licensing agreement which gives her strict control over how her image can be used."

Sunny Hostin stated, "I am thrilled to be a part of how top-quality AI productions cannot only enable writers and directors to have their imaginations unleashed and no longer be tethered to budgetary constraints, but I am excited to be able to help pioneer a new art form which can open up new dimensions for how public personalities can engage with audiences."

Sunny Hostin, continued, "To be able to bring my novels to life in movie and TV form, and actually have my image inserted in the productions, so that audiences can relate to me through my stories beyond my role as an author, is incredibly exciting to me. This entire generational innovation in filmmaking from Fountain 0 gives me confidence that AI can give me a way to both more fully develop, and more fully immerse myself in, IP I have developed. I feel particularly strongly that there is a need to bring stories to the big screen that are more in tune with the lives of diverse audiences that Hollywood focuses too little on, and I believe Fountain 0's AI productions can have a major impact on responding to the interests of these underserved audiences."

Pooya Koosha, also post- producer of the films, stated, "Our ability to refine image generation to not only present the physical likeness of a personality, but to match their voice and other characteristics will give fans a real sense that their favorite talents are actually present in the productions despite the fact that they will be synthetic images."

Tom Rogers stated, "Our approach is to make sure all persons whose images are used in any Fountain 0 production are compensated by receiving a revenue participation in the film. Even small parts which might not involve incorporating major personalities will participate in the revenue generated by any film for which their image is used.

Rogers continued, "With Sunny not only being a personality in front of the camera, but an author as well, we look forward to the potential to develop films based on her books. Writers and directors will have quite significant revenue participation in the productions they create. In that sense Sunny will participate as both a producer/writer in the revenue generated from any film but also participate in the film's upside from her image appearing in the film as well."

Emma Sarah Wilson, Counsel to Fountain 0, said the company has developed a comprehensive licensing framework governing the use of an individual's image. Wilson explained, "We have developed a robust long-form licensing agreement for every individual whose image, likeness and voice may be used in a Fountain 0 production. The agreement provides clear consent and usage rights, while establishing safeguards for how reference images and voice recordings are stored and used within the studio and its projects. Our goal is to protect each individual's privacy and control over their identity while preserving the creative flexibility and technical quality required to produce the highest quality image and voice generation."

Ash Koosha called for all influencers and those with major social media followings to join the Fountain 0 talent directory from which their likeness can be licensed. He stated, "If one's image or likeness is licensed with approval, a person becomes eligible to earn from what will be a fountain of film and tv episodes." Sign up here https://join.fountain0.com. 

Dreams of Violets is now streaming at Watch.Fountain0.com, and the trailer for Odysseus: The Fall is also available on the site as well. Interested viewers can sign up now to be on the list for advanced viewing of Odysseus: The Fall, scheduled for release next month.

Sold-out Huizhou premiere marks the first YUELAIMEI Hokkien-language song concert staged in mainland China outside the language's place of origin

HUIZHOU, China, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On the evening of August 21, the Hokkien Music & Culture Global Tour • 2026 Original Hokkien Song Concert took the stage at the Opera House of the Huizhou Culture and Art Center in Guangdong, China. Tickets sold out the moment they went on sale, filling all 1,300-plus seats in the hall. The performance was streamed live to audiences worldwide.

Hokkien is one of the 60 major world languages recognized by the United Nations. It originated in the southern Fujian Province and the eastern Guangdong Province in China. Hokkien speakers are a maritime people, distinct in culture from the land-based traditions of China's other communities. The language carries a thousand years of seafaring, exploration, and migration. Through the ports of Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, Xiamen, and Zhanglin in Shantou, Hokkien culture took root across Fujian and Guangdong, linked both sides of Taiwan, China, and spread far overseas. Today, the language faces a generational break in transmission among young people. With several hundred thousand Hokkien speakers living in Huizhou, efforts to revitalize the mother tongue carry real urgency here.

From Boston to Huizhou

The event was initiated by Hokkien Music & Culture, founded by Jiayu (Kitty) Huang, whose family home is in Huizhou. Raised by elders who insisted she keep her mother tongue, she went on to study in Massachusetts from a young age, training in composition and music production under noted professors from the New England Conservatory and Berklee College of Music. She began writing and producing music in sixth grade and has since contributed to several hundred works; in tenth grade, she received an Honorable Mention from the Massachusetts Composition Competition. She completed her undergraduate studies at the Thornton School of Music at the University of Southern California, where she founded and led the university's only Chinese traditional music ensemble. An advocate for Hokkien language preservation as a public-interest cause, she established Hokkien Music & Culture in the Hollywood district of Los Angeles in 2023 to promote and pass on Hokkien culture through music.

Hokkien Music & Culture's work spans music composition, record releases, and cultural promotion. The company regularly organizes Hokkien-language preservation events, including songwriting and literary competitions, concerts, cultural symposia, and academic paper awards. It also publishes and promotes Hokkien songs and literature with the aim of developing new talent in both fields. Since 2024, Hokkien Music & Culture has run a global Hokkien songwriting competition and a worldwide concert tour out of Los Angeles, drawing on charitable support to protect and grow the mother tongue.

Three Generations on One Stage

The concert brought together scholars of Hokkien culture from China and abroad, veteran musicians, and inheritors of intangible cultural heritage, with performers spanning three generations. Zhang Shenghuan, associate professor at the School of Music of Jimei University, wove Gaojia Opera vocal technique into her songs. Xiamen TV host Chen Xiaoyuan and UFO Records signed artist Zheng Lili performed several Hokkien classics songs. Huizhou's own heritage traditions were represented by Zhang Xiying, vice chair of the municipal musicians' association, who folded elements of Huidong fishermen's songs into her Hokkien performance. Shantou musician Jiang Shengxin, Teochew singer Du Weikun, Xiamen vocalists Zeng Zhichao and Chen Shuna, and Shantou singer Lin Yini shared the stage with the Huizhou Mengshen Chorus, passing the songs of home from one generation of musicians to the next.

The program balanced new original work with beloved standards. Winning entries from the 2024 and 2025 editions of the Global Hokkien Songwriting Competition were performed, including "Over Rivers and Mountains to Baizhang Stream," "A New Shirt," "Kapok," and "Take It Easy" — new melodies telling Hokkien stories. Familiar classics such as "Don't Lose Heart," "Old Love Lingers On," "Sea Waves," and "Words After Drinking" were presented in fresh arrangements. The Mengshen Chorus performed "Longing for the Spring Breeze" and "When the Flower Leaves the Branch," showcasing the warmth and quiet strength of the Hokkien songbook and drawing a strong emotional response from the audience.

Organizers and Academic Support

The concert was presented by Hokkien Music & Culture, with the Huizhou Dongjiang Hokkien Culture Research Association and Yifan Yinghua Culture Communication (Xiamen) Co., Ltd. as co-organizers. Hokkien Music & Culture (USA) and the Chinese Musicians Association of Boston supported international outreach. The evening was hosted in three languages—Hokkien, Mandarin, and English—and streamed live worldwide, carrying Hokkien culture beyond geographic borders. Scholars of the Hokkien language include Zhou Changji of Xiamen University and Dong Zhongsi of National Tsing Hua University in Taiwan, and Gan Yu'en of Jinan University served as cultural advisors, lending academic weight to the preservation effort.

Reception

The concert was a resounding success. It is understood to be the first Hokkien-language song concert ever staged in mainland China outside the language's place of origin, and major media outlets gave it extensive coverage. Zhou Changji, professor at Xiamen University and a leading authority on Hokkien culture in China, attended the performance. He said it was the most stirring Hokkien song concert he had seen in his life, praising the high caliber of the performers and the deeply moving response from the audience—proof, he said, of how much the mother tongue still means to the people who came.

Looking Ahead

Following two editions of the Global Hokkien Songwriting Competition in 2024 and 2025 and the 2025–2026 Hokkien Music & Culture Original Hokkien Song Global Tour, with stops in Boston, USA, and Huizhou, China, the company will continue to invest in Hokkien music creation and expand its channels of distribution at home and abroad, bringing new life to a thousand-year-old culture in a new era.

About Hokkien Music & Culture

Founded in Los Angeles in 2023, Hokkien Music & Culture works in music composition, record releases, and cultural promotion, with a mission to preserve and revitalize the Hokkien language through songwriting competitions, concerts, publications, and academic programs.

releases.title: Jon Batiste to Narrate American Amazon, Bringing His Signature Voice to Epic Giant Screen Documentary Featuring the South's Wildest Secrets
releases.body:
New film from Grizzly Creek Films, PBS and distributed by MacGillivray Freeman Films, opens in select IMAX and giant screen theaters starting November 13

LAGUNA BEACH, Calif., Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MacGillivray Freeman Films, the world's leading independent producer and distributor of giant screen films, announced today that acclaimed musician, composer, and storyteller Jon Batiste will narrate and serve as Executive Producer on American Amazon, the sweeping new documentary from Grizzly Creek Films and The WNET Group's award-winning Nature series for PBS. The feature film is slated to premiere in select IMAX® and giant screen theaters and museums beginning November 13, 2026, and the two-part Nature mini-series will release on PBS in early 2027.

Batiste's distinctive voice and deeply expressive artistry will guide audiences through one of North America's least explored and biologically rich regions—the vast network of wetlands spanning Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, and the Carolinas. A Louisiana native, Batiste brings a powerful emotional resonance to this immersive journey, elevating the film's celebration of nature, culture, and human connection to the ecosystem.

Four years in the making, American Amazon reveals an ancient and mysterious landscape defined by towering two-thousand-year-old cypress trees, labyrinthine flooded forests, a network of wild rivers, and an astonishing array of wildlife. From the mass migration of swallow-tailed kites—the world's only social raptor—to the elusive behaviors of American black bears in the swamp, the film uncovers a world teeming with life, discovery, and enduring surprises.

"Jon Batiste brings the American Amazon to life; his creativity, passion, and energy invite us to fall in love with this wild and mysterious place that is truly the world's best kept secret," said the film's director, writer, and co-producer Eric Bendick of Grizzly Creek Films. "His voice is a perfect match for all the drama and soul-stirring beauty of this landscape, allowing audiences to connect with the untamed spirit of the wild South."

Drawing on the filmmakers' extensive exploration in the region, American Amazon presents a remarkable collection of natural history stories—many never before captured on film. Together with Batiste's narration, the film offers an experience that is both epic in scale and deeply personal.

"Jon's ability to move between joy, wonder, and reflection makes him an ideal narrator for this story," said co-producer Thomas Winston of Grizzly Creek Films. "He brings a unique perspective that amplifies the film's message of appreciation and stewardship. American Amazon marks an exciting new chapter in our ongoing collaboration with Jon—and there's more to come."

"American Amazon shines a light on one of the most ecologically important and least understood regions in North America," said Fred Kaufman, Executive Producer of Nature. "Jon brings a rare authenticity to this story. His voice captures not only the wonder of the natural world, but also the deep cultural connection between the people, places, and wildlife that make the American South so extraordinary."

"I love introducing people to the swamp. Growing up in Louisiana, I've always felt a deep connection to the landscapes, culture, and spirit of my home," said Jon Batiste. "I think the South is sacred soil. American Amazon reveals the wild side that many people have never seen. It's a world of extraordinary beauty, mystery, and life – hiding right in our own backyard. We're celebrating the power of nature, creativity, and human connection – and this is just the beginning!"

Jon Batiste is an eight-time Grammy, Academy, and Emmy Award–winning singer, songwriter, composer, and pianist known for his genre-defying music. His 2025 album, Big Money, won the Grammy Award for Best Americana Album. In film, Batiste will next compose the score for Amazon MGM's The Thomas Crown Affair, directed by Michael B. Jordan. From 2015 to 2022, he served as bandleader and musical director of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

"Having worked with Jon previously on our giant screen film America's Musical Journey, I've seen firsthand the incredible artistry and range he brings to every project," said Shaun MacGillivray, President of MacGillivray Freeman Films. "He is an extraordinary talent, and his ability to connect with audiences through music and storytelling makes him the perfect voice for American Amazon."

More than a visual spectacle, American Amazon is a celebration of a fragile and irreplaceable ecosystem—and a call to action to protect this landscape – before it's too late. By sharing the region's untold stories and extraordinary biodiversity, the film aims to inspire audiences to reconnect with nature and recognize the importance of preserving these vital landscapes for future generations.

With MacGillivray Freeman Films leading distribution, American Amazon will roll out to leading science centers, museums, and giant screen theaters beginning November 2026.

About Grizzly Creek Films

Grizzly Creek Films specializes in filmmaking that marries compelling storytelling, dynamic characters, and unparalleled imagery. From their home base in Montana to locations around the world, the company produces films defined by authentic emotion, heart-pounding action, and breathtaking natural wonders.

About Nature

Since 1982, Nature has pioneered a television genre that is now widely emulated in the broadcast industry, bringing the natural world to millions of viewers. The series has won more than 800 honors from the television industry, the international wildlife film communities and environmental organizations, including 21 Emmys and three Peabodys. Nature is available for streaming concurrent with broadcast on all station-branded PBS platforms, including PBS.org and the PBS App, available on iOS, Android, Roku streaming devices, Apple TV, Android TV, Amazon Fire TV, Samsung Smart TV, Chromecast and VIZIO. Classic episodes are available on various FAST channel platforms and on PBS Passport. Nature is a production of The WNET Group.

About MacGillivray Freeman Films

MacGillivray Freeman Films is the world's foremost independent producer and distributor of original giant screen films for IMAX® and other large-format theaters. For more than 50 years, the company has been creating immersive, visually stunning films designed to educate, entertain, and inspire audiences around the globe. Its films have won numerous international awards including two Academy Award® nominations and three films inducted into the IMAX Hall of Fame, including Everest, the highest grossing giant screen documentary film of all time. MacGillivray Freeman's films are known for their artistry and celebration of science and the natural world. It is the first documentary film company to reach the one-billion-dollar benchmark for worldwide box office.

KINGSTON, ON, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Keynote speaker, facilitator, and JUNO Award–nominated singer-songwriter Peter Katz has been inducted into the National Speakers Association's (NSA) CPAE® Speaker Hall of Fame (only the fifth Canadian speaker in the award's history to receive the honour).

The Council of Peers Award for Excellence (CPAE®) is awarded by peers through a rigorous evaluation process that examines a speaker's integrity, message, delivery, and body of work over a career, and is reserved for those who have reached the top of the profession. Past honourees include Jim Rohn, Colin Powell, and Zig Ziglar.

Katz received the award at the NSA's annual conference awards banquet on July 27, 2026, in Austin, Texas, surrounded by family, dear friends, and colleagues.

Today, Peter is a trusted partner to Fortune 500 companies, leading healthcare systems, major associations, and all levels of government, all of whom turn to him to help clarify what matters most, recognize it in everyday actions, and celebrate it in ways that fuel connection and performance.

MEET PETER

Peter Katz is a Hall of Fame Keynote Speaker and a JUNO Award– and Canadian Screen Award–nominated singer-songwriter, and xchange Approach certified facilitator. He's built his career as an expert in helping teams recognize, value, and celebrate their individual and collective impacts. His interactive Celebrate What Matters™ Keynote Concerts feature songs and stories of resiliency, authenticity, and unexpected joy that ignite connection, foster belonging, and create momentum.

Katz is the founder of Heartstrings Songwriting Retreats, which allows aspiring songwriters of all experience levels to realize their lifelong dream of writing and recording their own song. He's also the co-founder of The Conscious Leaders Quest, an immersive five-day retreat in Costa Rica that invites a holistic approach to mind, body, and business, equipping leaders to do the vital inner work that transforms the way they lead.

GRATITUDE

Katz is quick to credit the honour to a process, not a performance. "This award is a recognition and celebration of a process," he said in his acceptance speech. "The process of seeing human beings and honouring the privilege of serving them with great care. That is what I have loved doing my whole life, as a songwriter, speaker and facilitator: shining a light on people's goodness and brilliance and then celebrating it as a way to inspire others."

He thanked the National Speakers Association and the community of peers who championed him along the way, along with the team at Speakers Spotlight who believed in him from the beginning. He reserved his warmest thanks for his family — including his partner, Taes, and his mother, Catherine, who were in the room for the induction.

Peter is particularly honoured to be inducted alongside his remarkable colleagues Manley Feinberg, Jessica Pettitt, Anton Gunn, and Allison Shapira.

LOS ANGELES, Aug. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- To mark Women's Equality Day in the United States, She Is The Music and ROSTR today released Music's Gender Parity Index, a new report finding that women account for fewer than 30% of creators on the rosters of record labels, music publishers, management companies, and booking agencies.

That underrepresentation extends to the professionals representing creators, with women comprising just 26.7% of managers and 25.9% of agents—revealing an imbalance at the economic core of the music industry.

Powered by ROSTR's music industry data, the analysis covers more than 500 companies and professionals across the IP-generating creator economy—from record labels and publishers to management companies and booking agencies. It also identifies 63 qualifying companies and professionals whose rosters comprise at least 50% women, collectively recognized as the 50% Club.

Why it matters:

Roster decisions influence which ideas receive capital, teams, distribution, global reach, licensing opportunities, performance opportunities, and the chance to generate long-term economic value. When women are underrepresented on these rosters, the industry risks underinvesting in creative voices, audiences, cultural perspectives, and revenue opportunities that could strengthen the entire music ecosystem.

Key findings from ROSTR's dataset include:

  • Women represent just 29.7% of rostered IP-generating creators, fewer than three in ten.
  • Women comprise 26.7% of managers and 25.9% of agents.
  • Scale is not the barrier: three qualifying agencies with rosters of more than 100 creators have crossed the 50% threshold.
  • Women have accounted for roughly 35% of new representation deals each year since 2023, indicating that recent progress has plateaued.
  • Among those new representation deals, women's share of management signings has remained relatively steady at around 39%, while their share of new label signings has fallen from 38.4% in 2023 to 34.3% through July 10, 2026. In publishing, women account for just 27.8% of new deals.

Parity is already being achieved: one in eight qualifying companies and professionals has a roster comprising at least 50% women. In total, 63 qualifying companies and professionals have reached that threshold, demonstrating that balanced rosters are achievable across business models, markets, and roster sizes. Together, they form the 50% Club.

"The imbalance we see on charts, festival stages and credits starts long before the spotlight—it starts with who gets signed, represented, and backed," said Laura Segura, Executive Director of She Is The Music. "This report looks upstream at those career-shaping decisions, because more equitable rosters can change both the creativity and the economics of music."

Leading the way:

The report ranks the qualifying companies and professionals with the highest share of women on their creator rosters, across recording, songwriting, production, and multiple disciplines. This includes the industry's largest rosters across agencies, major labels, and music publishers (including CAA and WME among agencies and Concord, Kobalt, and BMG among publishers).

Some key takeaways include:

  • CAA (38.6%), Universal Music Group (34.2%), and Concord (35.8%) have the highest shares of women on their rosters in their respective categories.
  • Among the 10 highest-ranked agencies with rosters of at least 100 creators, three have rosters comprising at least 50% women: TBA Agency at 55.6%, Luger at 53.6%, and Select Music at 50.4%.
  • All 10 of the highest-ranked management companies with rosters of at least 15 creators have reached or exceeded parity, led by Sandbox Entertainment at 66.7% women.
  • Nine individual managers with rosters of at least 10 creators have reached or surpassed parity, led by Sebastien LeTellier of Raw Material at 81.8%. Cherie Lily of Voss Management, Jason Owen of Sandbox Entertainment, and Max Gousse of Artistry Group each have rosters comprising 64.3% women.
  • Mouthwatering Records is the only qualifying record label with a roster of at least 30 creators in which women constitute a majority, at 55.9%.
  • Five qualifying music publishers have rosters that are at least 50% women, with Terrorbird at 68.8% and Killphonic at 57.9%.

The North Star: Progress Toward Parity

To advance gender parity, the report proposes five commitments, detailed in the full report, for companies that sign, represent, employ, or invest in talent.

The report sets an aspirational benchmark of gender parity by 2030 wherever roster mathematics make that achievable. Where existing roster size and turnover make standing-roster parity unattainable by 2030, the commitment should be equally concrete: measure progress, set credible benchmarks, broaden outreach, expand pathways, and be transparent.

"ROSTR is proud to partner with She Is The Music on this report, which surfaces a hard truth: women make up only 29.7% of rostered IP-generating creators," said Katie Holmes, COO of The ROSTR Group. "To help close that gap, we're pledging $63,000 in ROSTR Pro subscriptions to support She Is The Music's work in honor of the 63 companies and professionals already in the 50% Club, where each company roster is made up of at least 50% women. This pledge will grow every time another company joins the 50% club."  

About ROSTR

ROSTR is the music industry's intelligence platform — making the people, deals, and infrastructure of music searchable, verifiable, and current. Used daily by managers, agents, A&Rs, executives, and bookers across the global music business. Co-founded by Mark Williamson, formerly of Spotify's Artist Services team. For more information, visit hq.rostr.cc.

About She Is The Music

She Is The Music is a global nonprofit organization that convenes and advances the women's movement in music. The organization works to increase the number of women working, leading, and thriving across all areas of the industry. Through mentorship, education, research, and community, She Is The Music brings together creators, executives, and companies to help build a more inclusive music industry that better reflects the world it serves. She Is The Music was co-founded in 2018 by Alicia Keys, Jody Gerson, Ann Mincieli, and Sam Kirby Yoh. For more information, visit sheisthemusic.org.

Figures reflect roster composition within ROSTR's dataset as of July 10, 2026 and should not be interpreted as a census of the worldwide music industry. Definitions, eligibility criteria, limitations, and correction procedures are provided in the full 2026 Music's Gender Parity Index. Data corrections may be submitted to data@rostr.cc.

TORONTO, Aug. 26, 2026 /CNW/ -- As the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) returns, RBC is marking its 19-year legacy as major partner with a line-up of festival-favourite activations and events designed to celebrate the ideas that shape culture, transform perspectives and connect communities.

RBC House continues to be the leading destination for film and industry parties throughout the festival, and will host events featuring some of the festival's most anticipated premieres. Located at Petros82 restaurant in the heart of Toronto's Entertainment District, the space will also feature the Los Angeles Times Studio presented by RBC for its fifth year, offering a dedicated space to capture video interviews, photo portraits and compelling content with some of the biggest names at TIFF.

The RBC Red Carpet Gallery is back as one of the most coveted spots for celebrity spotting during TIFF, putting film fans front and centre on the red carpet. Located at David Pecaut Square (215 King Street West, Toronto) along the Roy Thomson Hall red carpet, the activation gives Avion Rewards Elite, Premium and Select members prime access to watch stars step out for their Gala premieres. Guests will receive a swag bag upon arrival (while supplies last), along with a chance to win a grand prize of 25,000 Avion Rewards points and more. Avion Rewards Elite and Premium members can reserve their spot in advance at https://rbctiff.com/ – registration is first-come, first-served and space is limited. Avion Rewards Select members and the general public can join via a same-day rush line, subject to available capacity.

The TIFF Black Excellence Brunch presented by RBC returns for the fourth consecutive year, continuing its legacy of recognizing, honouring and celebrating emerging Canadian talent and inclusivity in film. The gathering provides opportunities to connect, share and collectively grow by bringing together voices from the local and global film community.

For the second year, RBC is proud to be an Official Supporting Partner of the TIFF Tribute Awards Gala, taking place on September 13. A cornerstone of the Festival calendar, the Gala is an annual fundraiser dedicated to advancing TIFF's year-round programming and its mission of broadening perspectives through the art of film. The evening honours standout contributors to entertainment – from accomplished actors and directors to emerging creators making their mark on the industry.

Beyond the festival, RBC is a long-standing supporter of creatives, equipping the next generation of talent with the tools, connections and opportunities needed to build lasting careers, while championing greater inclusivity and prosperity in communities across the country. Through RBC's ongoing collaboration with TIFF, the Share Her Journey Initiative has opened meaningful doors for women creators in screen-based storytelling, closing gaps at the production and industry-access level through more deliberate infrastructure for visibility, mentorship and career advancement.

LOS ANGELES, Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Firebird, a powerful short film inspired by the true story of a human trafficking survivor, premiered at the HollyShorts Film Festival, one of the world's premier Academy Award® and BAFTA-qualifying film festivals.

The film showcases the horrors of human trafficking through the true story of Dolma, a human trafficking survivor who, twenty years ago, was manipulated and sold into human trafficking.
